title: SIGEM: A Simple yet Effective Similarity based Graph Embedding Method

problem.claim: Existing graph embedding methods have drawbacks involving global graph structure, learning quality, directed-graph degree distributions, and applicability.

gap.claim: The described drawbacks motivate a graph similarity measure and embedding method applicable across directed and undirected graphs with improved scalability.

contributions.claim: LINOW is a recursive link-based graph similarity measure that uses node weights and applies to directed and undirected graphs.
A non-approximate matrix formulation and single-node and batch-node variants are provided to accelerate and scale LINOW computation.

SIGEM is a self-supervised, contrastive-free, similarity-based graph embedding method that ranks nodes using LINOW-bn and preserves those ranks in embedding vectors through a single-layer neural network.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on eight real-world datasets and comparisons with thirteen state-of-the-art and conventional embedding methods reportedly show that LINOW-sn and LINOW-bn improve the scalability of naive LINOW.
The authors report that LINOW benefits similarity-based graph embedding.
The authors report that SIGEM achieves the highest accuracy in graph reconstruction and node classification and significantly outperforms other methods in most link prediction cases.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph embedding methods are established in the literature.
The authors identify four drawbacks of existing methods.
LINOW is introduced as a recursive similarity measure for directed and undirected graphs.
A matrix form and node-level variants are introduced to accelerate and scale similarity computation.
SIGEM uses LINOW-bn and rank preservation for embedding, followed by comparative experiments across datasets and tasks.

source_observation.claim: The method combines a graph similarity measure, scalable computation variants, and rank preservation in a single-layer embedding model.

interpretation.claim: Separating similarity computation from scalable implementation variants can support embedding designs that preserve a defined structural ordering.

application.claim: For graph representation tasks, consider explicitly modeling node similarity and preserving its ranking in the learned representation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported datasets, methods, and tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the mathematical definition of LINOW or its matrix formulation.
The abstract does not provide dataset identities, experimental settings, accuracy values, or statistical analyses.
The abstract does not describe computational costs, model hyperparameters, or failure cases.
